cap1.mp3: Sophia takes the 740 train every morning. She always sits in the same siet. On Monday, there is a small brown notebook on it. There is no name on the front, and there is no phone number. The notebook is old, and it is nearly full. Sophia waits, but nobody comes back for it. The train is at her station, so she puts the notebook in her bag.
cap2.mp3: At work, Sophia opens the notebook. The first page is a short list, bread, milk, six eggs. Next to the eggs, there is a small drawing of an egg. Six eggs is a lot of eggs for a list with three things on it. Under the list, there is one more line, but Sophia cannot read it. The writing is very small and very fast.
cap3.mp3: On page four, there is a drawing of a cat. It is a very bad drawing, but it is a cat. Under the cat, there is one line, Sunday. He is still not eating. Sophia looks at her phone. Today is Monday. She closes the notebook and then she opens it again.
cap4.mp3: Near the end, there is an address, but the page is wet. The name of the street is gone. One thing is still black. The number, 73. Sophia knows the three streets near the station. Only one of them has a number 73 because the other two stop at 40. She looks at the clock. Her train home is at 610, so she does not go to the station. She walks.
cap5.mp3: Number 73 is a small house with a red door. An old man opens it. Sophia gives him the notebook. He does not say thank you. He says, page four? I write everything down because I forget things. Then he takes her to the kitchen. The cat is asleep in a big box next to the heater. He ate this morning, says the man. He only eats egg. On Sunday, he was not eating, but I bought six. Why six? Because he is going to eat them. In the end, Sophia misses the 610 and she is not sorry.
